readmeHtml:
An agent meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex.


Run your first task

Run this in your project folder:

npx ruflo@latest init

Then open Claude Code in the same folder and give it a real task, for example:

Use a ruflo swarm to review this repo: find the riskiest module, write tests for it, and summarise what you changed.

init adds ruflo's agents, hooks, memory and MCP server to the project, and Claude Code picks them up on its next start. Codex and other MCP clients work too: point them at npx -y ruflo@latest mcp start.

Check the result. Ask the agent to name the module it chose, show the test it added, and report the test command and result. Review the diff in your project.

First task walkthrough · Inspect a run in Mission Control · Other ways to install

Other ways to install

There are two different install paths with very different surface areas. Pick based on what you need (#1744):

Claude Code Plugin CLI install (npx ruflo init)
What it gives you Slash commands + a few skills + agent definitions per-plugin Full Ruflo loop — 98 agents, 60+ commands, 30 skills, MCP server, hooks, daemon
Files in your workspace Zero .claude/, .claude-flow/, CLAUDE.md, helpers, settings
MCP server registered Only if ruflo-core is installed (it ships its own .mcp.json) — most other plugins don't Yes
Hooks installed No Yes
Best for Try a single plugin's commands without committing to the full install Production use — everything works as documented

Claude Code plugins only. This route installs core tools, the visual console and runtime mods, with no files added to your project. It needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later. Run inside Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-console@ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-mods@ruflo
/reload-plugins
/ruflo

From a terminal, on Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: claude plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo --marketplace ruvnet/ruflo. Mods run with your account's permissions, so review their code before installing.

Codex or another MCP client, without project setup. Configure the command npx with the arguments ["-y", "ruflo@latest", "mcp", "start"]. To set up a project interactively, run npx ruflo@latest init wizard.

Plain terminal. The console also runs on its own, without Claude Code: npx ruflo tui. Add --plain to print one frame for scripts. See the terminal UI guide.

ruflo-core registers its own MCP server. Its tools use the mcp__plugin_ruflo-core_ruflo__ prefix.

CLI Install

macOS / Linux / WSL / Git-Bash:

# One-line install (POSIX shells only — see Windows note below)
curl -fsSL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ruvnet/ruflo@main/scripts/install.sh | bash

All platforms (including native Windows PowerShell / cmd):

# Interactive setup wizard — runs identically on every platform
npx ruflo@latest init wizard

# Quick non-interactive init
# npx ruflo@latest init

# Or install globally
npm install -g ruflo@latest

💡 Windows users: the curl ... | bash form needs a POSIX shell (Git-Bash, WSL, MSYS). The npx ruflo@latest init wizard line works natively in PowerShell and cmd. If you hit an 'bash' is not recognized error, use the npx line instead — both end up running the same init flow.

MCP Server

# Add Ruflo as an MCP server in Claude Code
claude mcp add claude-flow -- npx ruflo@latest mcp start

For static inspection of local applications and binaries, see the ruRE plugin guide.

Grok Build: npx ruflo init --grok writes the project host surface (.grok/, the team bus, and the operator guide) and nothing outside the project; add --dry-run to preview. Setup, the spawn_subagent contract, the optional status row, and what to re-check when Grok updates: the Grok operator guide.

Mission Control

Open /ruflo in Claude Code to monitor agent work, inspect a run, or give Claude permission to operate the console.

If you use the console, open the agent’s log and compare its actions with the diff and test result from your first task.

Task What you can do
Monitor work Track workflows, agents, models, token use, and cost. Workflow demo with sample data
Inspect a run Search logs and results, triage failures, replay a run, and compare outcomes.
Customize the console Preview Orbital, switch among six palettes, save a theme, or import its JSON. 38 second renderer replay · Theme Studio guide
Control Claude’s access Choose a permission level and approval mode in Settings → Claude control. Review each action in the live log. Permission details

Install and open the console

Use Claude Code 2.1.287 or later. Review mods before installing them because they run with your account’s permissions.

/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-console@ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-mods@ruflo
/reload-plugins

Open /plugin to check the active mods, then /ruflo to launch the console. For a project initialized through the CLI, run npx ruflo init and restart Claude Code before opening /ruflo.

Console mods and catalog
Mod Purpose
ruflo-console Opens the console beside Claude Code.
ruflo-mods Routes prompts and enforces policy in process.
ruflo-swarm Adds a pane showing the swarm.
ruflo-ruos Adds the ruOS status segment.

Open /ruflo market to inspect plugins, mods, and skills. The catalog asks for confirmation before installing, enabling, disabling, or updating an item.

Create a mission with Claude

The default is read + ask. Available levels are read, write, manage, and full, with ask or auto approval. Actions above the selected level are refused. Network, spending, and destructive actions require confirmation even in auto.

  1. In Settings → Claude control, select write + ask.
  2. Ask Claude, “Create a mission to add a dark mode toggle. Show me the mission and its status.”
  3. Confirm the pending creation request. Check Missions for the goal and Overview for the action log. This verifies that the mission was created.
  4. Select Take back control, then ask Claude to take another console action. The console should refuse it until you restore access.

Watch the recorded Claude Haiku session to see mission creation, page navigation, a refused swarm stop, and control being taken back. The recording uses write + auto. Step 1 uses ask so you can approve creation yourself. Recorded test findings · Reproduction script

How Ruflo works

Agent = Model + Harness. The model writes; the harness gives it tools, memory, loops, sandboxes, and controls so it can actually work. Ruflo is the harness — the execution layer around Claude Code and Codex that adds 100+ specialized agents, coordinated swarms, self-learning memory, federated comms across machines, and enterprise security guardrails. So agents don't just run, they collaborate.

What can the next run reuse?

Useful trajectories and task feedback can inform future work. Results depend on the configured memory, learning components and quality of feedback. Learning plugin.

Watch the learning walkthrough · Local RVF search recipe

Conceptual learning loop. Local vector retrieval and contrastive updates can run without an LLM; embeddings and configured learning modules are still required. See the RuVector training integration and trajectory contrastive learning.

How do two teams exchange work?

Slack gave teams channels. Federation gives agents the same thing — shared workspaces across trust boundaries, where agents on different machines, orgs, or cloud regions can discover each other, prove who they are, and collaborate on tasks.

The difference: some channels are trusted, some aren't. @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation handles that automatically. Your agents join a federation, get verified via mTLS + ed25519, and start exchanging work — with PII stripped before anything leaves your node and every message auditable. Untrusted agents can still participate at lower privilege: they see discovery info, not your memory. As they prove reliable, trust upgrades. If they misbehave, they get downgraded instantly — no human in the loop required.

You don't configure handshakes or manage certificates. You federation init, federation join, and your agents start talking. The protocol handles identity, the PII pipeline handles data safety, and the audit trail handles compliance.

📘 Full user guide: docs/federation/ — setup, MCP tools, trust levels, circuit breaker, and the (opt-in) WireGuard mesh layer that ties packet-layer reachability to federation trust. ADR-111 deep-dive at docs/federation/phase7-mesh-bringup.md.

Federation capabilities
Capability How it works
🔒 Zero-trust federation Remote agents start untrusted. Identity proven via mTLS + ed25519 challenge-response. No API keys, no shared secrets.
🛡️ PII-gated data flow 14-type detection pipeline scans every outbound message. Per-trust-level policies: BLOCK, REDACT, HASH, or PASS. Adaptive calibration reduces false positives.
📊 Behavioral trust scoring Formula (0.4×success + 0.2×uptime + 0.2×threat + 0.2×integrity) continuously evaluates peers. Upgrades require history; downgrades are instant.
📋 Compliance built-in HIPAA, SOC2, GDPR audit trails as compliance modes. Every federation event produces a structured record searchable via HNSW.
🤝 9 MCP tools + 10 CLI commands Full lifecycle: federation_init, federation_send, federation_trust, federation_audit, and more.
Example: two teams sharing fraud signals without sharing customer data 
# Team A: initialize federation and generate keypair
npx claude-flow@latest federation init

# Team A: join Team B's federation endpoint
npx claude-flow@latest federation join wss://team-b.example.com:8443

# Team A: send a task — PII is stripped automatically before it leaves
npx claude-flow@latest federation send --to team-b --type task-request \
  --message "Analyze transaction patterns for account anomalies"

# Team A: check peer trust levels and session health
npx claude-flow@latest federation status

See issue #1669 for the complete architecture, trust model, and implementation roadmap.

# Claude Code plugin
/plugin install ruflo-federation@ruflo

# Or via CLI
npx claude-flow@latest plugins install @claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation

releases.body:
## 3.79.0: provenance-attested releases, pinned install output, Project Anatole on by default

This is the first ruflo release published from CI with **SLSA provenance**. `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow` and `ruflo` 3.79.0 each carry a SLSA v1 attestation built in `ruvnet/ruflo` by `stable-npm-release.yml`. `latest` moved only after the release gate confirmed that each attestation matches the verified archive's sha512 (ADR-545).

### Supply chain (ADR-545, #5048)
- **CI-only publishing:** the release train now publishes only from GitHub Actions with `npm publish --provenance`, and only from `main`. The workflow rehearses by default (dry run), and publishing requires `dry_run=false`.
- **Pinned `init` output:** `ruflo init` writes our packages at the CLI's own exact version (`npx -y ruflo@3.79.0 …`) instead of `@latest`. `--channel latest` keeps the old floating behaviour.
- **`ruflo init repin` (or `init --repin`):** moves an existing project's `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json`, CLAUDE.md and helpers onto the current version. It supports `--dry-run` and lists every changed line.
- **`ruflo doctor -c provenance`:** checks that the pinned version has a SLSA attestation from `ruvn

releases.name: v3.78.1 — SONA balanced-mode recall fix
releases.body:
## Fix

- **SONA balanced mode returns current, exact matches** (#5044). Balanced mode served pattern matches from a cache keyed on a lossy embedding hash. That cache could return stale patterns after an update, or a near-duplicate query's results. It is removed: balanced mode now does an exact scan with bounded top-k selection, so its recall matches a full sort. Ships via `@claude-flow/neural` 3.1.1.

## Packages

- `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.78.1 on `latest`
- `@claude-flow/neural` 3.1.1 on `latest`

Patch release on top of 3.77.1.

## Security
- Managed-agent tools refuse sessions this project did not create. The ownership ledger moved out of the workspace (`~/.claude-flow/managed/`), and terminate checks the provider's environment id. (#4831, fixes #4751; thanks @MannXo)
- The pre-bash root-delete guard reads `$(...)` substitutions and `${X:-/}` parameter defaults. (#4848 via #5024; thanks @MannXo)
- Federation envelopes get a freshness check and replay guard. (#4849 via #5022)

## Fixes
- The semantic router database stays under the memory root. (#4835)
- Memory exits non-zero when a refused sql.js save loses writes. (#4839)
- `init --dry-run` no longer performs a real init. (#4995)
- Pins `@claude-flow/aidefence@3.2.2`, which recovers HNSW entries the graph cannot reach. (#5018)
- ruflo-mods 0.17.1: `claude plugin validate` passes on Claude Code 2.1.323+. (#5017)

## Install
```
npx ruflo@3.77.2
```
`npm audit --omit=dev` on a fresh install matches 3.77.1 (7 high: zod, picomatch and agentic-flow chains, all tracked; zod 4 migration in #5021).

releases.name: v3.77.1 — AgentDB honours the configured embedding model
releases.body:
## 3.77.1

**Fix: AgentDB now honours the configured embedding model and dimension (#4984, #4985)**

`memory_store` ignored `.claude-flow/embeddings.json` after #2305: the controller registry created AgentDB with only a `dbPath`, so a configured model and dimension were dropped and AgentDB fell back to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at 384 dimensions.

- `@claude-flow/memory` 3.3.3 forwards the configured dimension to AgentDB and installs the configured embedder, rejecting vectors of the wrong length.
- The CLI memory bridge passes a local embedder when a non-default model is configured, and labels stored rows by the embedder that actually produced them.
- Stores pinned to the default 384-dimension model are unchanged.

Also merged: #4975 (quarantine a flaky browser suite on CI).

Known: `no-metaharness-smoke` and the console `write-argv` test (#4978) were red on main before this release.

Thanks to the reporter of #4984.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A streamlined, visual workflow automation engine for integrating cloud services and APIs.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Ruflo is an open-source workflow automation platform that allows users to connect various cloud applications and APIs using a visual, drag-and-drop interface. It processes events asynchronously, enabling complex data transformations and conditional logic between different interconnected services. The system is designed to be highly extensible, allowing developers to create custom nodes for proprietary internal APIs. It can be self-hosted, ensuring data privacy and compliance for enterprise use cases. By abstracting API communication, it empowers non-engineers to build powerful automated workflows.
keyFeatures: Visual workflow builder: Provides a drag-and-drop interface for designing complex logic without writing code.
Extensive integrations: Supports connecting to hundreds of popular SaaS applications and databases.
Custom node creation: Allows developers to write custom JavaScript to integrate proprietary systems.
Self-hosting capabilities: Enables deployment on internal servers to maintain strict data privacy.
Conditional logic: Supports branching, loops, and comprehensive error handling within the automated workflows.

useCases.title: Business process automation
useCases.description: Operations teams use it to automatically sync customer data between a CRM and a billing system.

useCases.title: Alerting and monitoring
useCases.description: Engineers configure workflows to send Slack notifications when a database metric exceeds a threshold.

useCases.title: Data transformation
useCases.description: Analysts create pipelines to extract data from an API, reformat it, and load it into a data warehouse.

useCases.title: Webhook handling
useCases.description: Developers utilize it to catch external webhooks and trigger internal serverless functions.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Operations teams, business analysts, and developers looking to automate repetitive tasks. It is ideal for organizations that require a powerful, self-hosted alternative to commercial automation tools.
